source.probe: advance-matched Liberation Serif derivative (tools/build-metric-fonts.py): hmtx = David DFonts advances exactly (Hebrew letters 0.78-1.29 of Liberation Serif per glyph, Latin a-z identical to Times, digits 0.886, space 0.885); Word paces David at its hhea 0.9839 (corpus 2026-11-03: 11 pt line 360 auto -> 16.3 pt)

note:
David (Windows Hebrew default, shipped inside Office) has no macOS copy, so
Chromium drew Hebrew runs in Lucida Grande / Helvetica, 10-20% wider, and
bulleted paragraphs wrapped one line more than Word (corpus 2026-11-03,
174 -> 184 pages). The ranged faces are advance-matched Liberation Serif
derivatives (Hebrew block, presentation forms, Latin-1, sheqel): David
advances in hmtx, outlines scaled horizontally per glyph. The rangeless
Liberation Serif faces cover the rest at 100% (David's Latin is Times-metric).
Every face pins David's hhea box 0.7349 / 0.2490 so the glyph box matches the
resolver's 0.9839 pitch. Word has no italic cut; both sides synthesize it.
